messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: residSE
parts:
Is there a method in aroma.affymetrix comparable to affyPLM::residSE?

What I'm after is the gene-wise standard errors for the model:

Y_gij = mu_gi + alpha_gj + e_gij

-mus are chip effects
-alphas are probe affinities

I want the estimate of var(e_gij), not SE(mu) or SE(alpha).

If not, I can just calculate it from the weights and residuals, but
just wondering if this has been done already. I suspect that these
don't get used too often (after all the other standard errors are
calculated).

Cheers,
Mark

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] residSE
parts:
Hi all.

OK, well, just ignore my posts regarding the residuals and residual
standard errors. I found some of Ken's old code and sorted it out.

In case any one needs this, I've written a function comparable to
residSE for PLMset objects as:

# pset is a PLMset object
vv<-residSE(pset)

# plm is an RmaPlm object
v<-aromaResidSE(plm)

plot(v[,1],vv[,1]) # showing the match b/w affyPLM and aroma.affymetrix


aromaResidSE<-function(plm) {
deconvolve<-function(u) {
log2(.subset2(.subset2(u,1),1))
}
rs<-calculateResiduals(plm,verbose=-10)
res<-readUnits(rs, stratifyBy="pm")
res<-lapply(res,deconvolve)
ws<-calculateWeights(plm,verbose=-10)
wts<-readUnits(ws, stratifyBy="pm")
wts<-lapply(wts,deconvolve)
vs<-matrix(,nrow=length(res.aa2),ncol=2)
for(i in 1:nrow(vs)) {
dm<-dim(wts[[i]])
df<-prod(dm)-dm[1]-dm[2]+1
vs[i,2]<-df
vs[i,1]<-sqrt(sum(wts[[i]]*res[[i]]^2)/df)
if(i %% 10000==0) print(i)
}
colnames(vs)<-c("Resid SE","df")
rownames(vs)<-names(wts)
vs[order(rownames(vs)),]
}

It obviously runs a lot faster if the calculateResiduals and
calculateWeights have been previously run.

Cheers,
Mark
